audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d says a wasted Blinding Dart is a 'fifteen-second invitation'. Blinding Dart is a flat 7 second cooldown at every rank.
audit.why: The error is in the dangerous direction: it doubles the window. A Mel player who steps up believing she has fifteen seconds of safety will be inside Teemo's range with the Dart already back up, and her empowered auto — the whole point of stepping up — gets blanked. Seven seconds is barely enough for one Q volley and a retreat.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart is 7s flat. The punish window is one rotation, not a stroll.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Q Blinding Dart cooldown 7, flat at all ranks)

audit.whatIsWrong: Blinding Dart is named as the matchup-defining threat in eleven places across both layers, and nowhere does either layer state that it is a projectile Rebuttal can reflect back onto Teemo.
audit.why: This is the best single piece of tech in the matchup and the entry hides it. Blinding Dart carries the projectile flag; Rebuttal reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker. A reflected Dart blinds Teemo — and Teemo's entire damage output routes through his basic attacks, since Toxic Shot is an on-hit effect. So the reflect does not merely save Mel's empowered auto, it turns off his. The content layer gestures at this once with 'eat his projectile and fling it back' but never names the Dart, so the player does not know which projectile is the one worth a 38s cooldown.
audit.corrected: Hold Rebuttal for Blinding Dart specifically — reflecting it blinds Teemo, and his damage is auto-attack based.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Q flags: projectile; E Toxic Shot flags: onHit, 'Each of Teemo's attacks will poison the target On-Hit')
champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W Rebuttal: reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] credits Teemo's kiting to 'passive move speed'. The move speed is Move Quick (W). Teemo's actual passive, Guerrilla Warfare, is invisibility and appears nowhere in either layer.
audit.why: Two costs. First, it mislabels the kiting tool, and Move Quick's passive speed drops the moment Teemo is struck by an enemy champion — which means Mel's Q ticks strip it. That is an actionable counter the entry never states. Second, calling the move speed 'passive' quietly buries the real passive: Teemo goes invisible standing still, and can move while invisible inside brush. Against a champion with no dash and no reveal, an invisible Teemo in a side brush is the thing that actually kills her, and the entry only ever warns about shrooms.
audit.corrected: Move Quick (W) is the speed and it breaks when he is hit. Guerrilla Warfare (P) is the invisibility, and it moves in brush.
sources: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (W Move Quick: 'passively increasing his Move Speed until he is struck by an enemy champion or turret'; P Guerrilla Warfare: invisible standing still, maintains invisibility while moving in brush)

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t all state Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26. Twenty is under the rank-5 floor and roughly half the rank-1 value. In this matchup specifically the cost is high, because W is also the answer to Blinding Dart — spending it on chip means eating every Dart for the next 38 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and report[0].t say 'Poke mirror you usually win'. The recorded win rate is 45% across 40 games — the largest sample in this slice — and content.win gives Teemo four of seven stages.
audit.why: The content layer says plainly 'This is where he pulls ahead' and 'I lose the lane long-term and I lose the map'. The full layer's headline says the opposite. On a 40-game sample there is no ambiguity about direction, and the headline is the first thing a player reads on the loading screen.
audit.corrected: Frame it as the reflect matchup it is: one real window at 6, and a lane that drifts to Teemo otherwise.
sources: champ-data/content/mel.js (win[] gives Teemo levels 3, 4-5, First item, 2+ items)

notes: Best matchup in the slice for data quality on the content side — the packet logged zero defects and every ability name is correct, so nearly all my edits here land on the full layer. The headline finding is that neither layer ever states that Rebuttal reflects Blinding Dart, despite Blinding Dart being named as the matchup-defining threat in eleven separate strings. It is a flagged projectile, Rebuttal reflects projectiles back at the attacker, and Teemo's whole damage profile is basic-attack based through Toxic Shot's on-hit — so the reflect blinds the one champion in the game who least wants to be blinded. That is the single most valuable line I added anywhere in this slice. PHASE SIDES UNTOUCHED, same length problem as the other Mel entries: full.phases gives Mel level 1 then 'Skill' for all six later stages, while content.win gives Teemo levels 3, 4-5, First item and 2+ items. Correcting 'Skill' (5 chars) to 'Teemo' (5 chars) would actually fit the length band here, unlike the Sylas entry — but I did not propose it because the phase .why text is generic Mel-favoured boilerplate ('Blackfire Torch spike — your volleys burn through sustain') that would then contradict its own side field. Fixing the sides without rewriting the whys would make the chart worse, and rewriting seven whys to a fixed length is a bigger change than I can justify on my own. Flagging for a deliberate pass. I nudged diffRating 5.5 to 6.5 and left diff as EVEN — 45% across 40 games is a real lean but not a hard counter, and I would rather under-correct than overstate it.
